h2. *Epic Goal*

* Change the lifecycle of the DevSpaces operator-based offering on OpenShift from currently rolling release to platform-agnostic, such that multiple release lines are available in parallel to customers

h2. *Why is this important?*

* Customers are forced to run the latest version of DevSpaces at all times which perceived as as unsuitable for production environments by customers, they have qualification cycles for new minor / major product versions of up to 6 months
* the rolling release tier is specifically providing a space for offerings that are based on nascent, fast moving upstream projects, which high change velocity where Red Hat is not the sole maintainer: this definition does not fit DevSpaces

h2. *Acceptance Criteria (Mandatory)*

* the DevSpaces operator support lifecycle model changes to the platform-agnostic model
* at least two release lines must be supported in parallel, giving customers time to prepare updates to newer major or minor versions - the exact number is up to the DevSpaces team
* all currently supported OpenShift versions must be covered by any of the parallel release sreams

h2.

The Q3 blog post for WTO is an introductory blog post that explains how WTO works to the user, as well as simple customizations with wtoctl: [https://developers.redhat.com/articles/2024/09/02/explore-full-capabilities-web-terminal-operator]

This issue tracks the completion of the Q4 blog post for WTO. This blog post can build on top of the Q3 blog post, by describing additional customizations the user can perform on their web terminal.

Some ideas are:
 * Show a dockerfile to further customize the WTO tooling image to use a custom shell (maybe fish or configure installed zsh) and have interesting quality of life cli tools.
 * Mount ssh keys so that private git repos (containing yaml templates for example) can be cloned

WTO 1.11 will provide a tooling container based on RHEL9, since this is supported by`oc` for OpenShift 4.16 

The following binaries that we ship in the WTO 1.10 tooling container may not run on RHEL9 based images:
||Binary||Slack thread||Related Jira issue||
|tkn|https://redhat-internal.slack.com/archives/CSPS1077U/p1721766396379289|https://issues.redhat.com/browse/SRVKP-4554|

Binaries that do not run on RHEL9 based containers should not be shipped in the WTO 1.11 tooling image, as there's no guarantee it works as intended.

Users for clusters with WTO 1.11 installed can still use these binaries if they change the WTO tooling image themselves to use WTO 1.10's tooling image [1] , or a custom image of their choice, when starting their terminal for the first time (see comment for example).

The Web Terminal Operator provides users with the ability to create a terminal instance embedded in the OpenShift Console. 

*BU Priority Overview*
The Web Terminal Operator provides excellent perations inside the cluster using the Developer console in a browser. It allows our customers to manage/administrate the OpenShift cluster from the box using the most popular built-in tools from the xterm js terminal directly from the browser instance of the OpenShift console.
This product is using ....customers //TODO add business info about real using (maybe obtain from PM)


*Goals*
*_Security control:_*
- According to the company security standards, we need to setup all scope of the security testing of WTO.  More details in the [document|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1O38OIZa4xn3FB8QIZYoaWWEr8PSz-dASX0F_n8iPLFY/edit]: 

*_Improve/Change quality automation and visibility_:*
- According to the CI Stability Quality Metric initiative, we should reorganize our test model and implement new tests using the appropriate test tool for reporting into the report portal and analyze the test results
*_//TODO_ other goals from PM and devs_*
 
* State of the Business*
*_//TODO_ need to obtain info from PM/Team lead about current business state_*
 
*Execution Plans*
* End of Q4:
- Pass the recommended security testing for all engineers in WTO team
- Find a solution for setting up security testing (provide real cluster with installing WebTerminal and run DAST scanner)
- Review RH-SDL Schedule and finish main security verifications for WTO
- Review acceptance test plan for WTO. Add/change tests if this need
- Find an appropriate test tool to provide clear quality metrics
- Create a dashboard on ReportPortal and find an agent for sending test data into ReportPortal

*References:*
[Security Schedule doc.|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1O38OIZa4xn3FB8QIZYoaWWEr8PSz-dASX0F_n8iPLFY/edit#heading=h.9dl8g1an0ie1]

items.toString:
According to the issue: https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHDP-720, we need to provide a reliable mechanism to round tests and send results to the RedHat report portal  for analyzing results, categorizing and interpreting results for the next actions.

 

I see two possible solutions:
1. The WTO project is based on the GO lang ecosystem, and ideally, it would be nice to apply GO test engine

2. If we are stuck or have some problems with this - we can use [https://github.com/eclipse/che] based on TypeScript currently; it provides all mechanisms for a run and sends results to the report portal.
